summary: Fire tower near Petersburg announced in 1929 and staffed in 1937 as Elkhorn, Hardy County; FFLA lists it standing. Name, county and later history unclear.

facts.status_note: FFLA list says standing; no later report found and not verified on the ground
facts.agency: State game and fish commission (construction in 1929)

events.note: Construction announced for a fire tower near Petersburg, Grant County, to start at once; completion not found
M.M. Friddle and Vance Belt stationed at the fire tower on Elkhorn for the fire season

evidence.supports: 1929 construction of a fire tower near Petersburg, Grant County, by the state game and fish commission
evidence.quote: Construction of a fire tower near Petersburg, Grant County, will be started at once by the state game and fish commission

evidence.supports: the 1929 item is from the Charleston Gazette
April 1937 item date; by April 1937 the tower was staffed
M.M. Friddle and Vance Belt stationed at the fire tower on Elkhorn in 1937
evidence.quote: M.M. Friddle and Vance Belt are now stationed at the fire tower on Elkhorn for the fire season

evidence.supports: the 1937 item is from the Cumberland Evening Times
the 1937 item places Elkhorn in Hardy County, as the only other Hardy tower is Big Ridge
evidence.quote: The only other fire tower in Hardy county is the Big Ridge tower in the Lost River State Park

evidence.supports: FFLA lists Elkhorn in Hardy County, standing, at 38.92887 -79.04576
Judy's county history uses Elk Horn Rock as a boundary landmark running to the Hardy and Pendleton line; a full-text search finds no mention of a tower
evidence.quote: to the top of Elk Horn Rock and continued along the top of the mountain to the Hardy and Pendleton Line

sources.title: History of Grant and Hardy Counties, West Virginia

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1929 item places construction near Petersburg, Grant County. The 1937 item and the FFLA list place the tower in Hardy County. We keep Hardy, which matches the record and the 1937 item, and flag the 1929 wording.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Status and coordinates come only from the FFLA list; no NHLR page for this tower is in the crawl cache. The Forest Lookouts page is the only source describing the tower itself, and it has no completion date or later history. Name and site are unclear: Forest Lookouts files it as Elk Horn Rock, FFLA as Elkhorn, and the Judy history uses Elk Horn Rock only as a boundary landmark. Check whether Elk Horn Rock and the Elkhorn tower are one site before merging records. The WV Division of Forestry article (wvforestry.com) does not name it. The Judy history's copyright line in the OCR text reads 'B, L, JUDY' while the title page reads 'E. L. JUDY'; the story uses E. L. Judy from the title page.
